module_name: Visualization and Dashboards: Networks, Time, Text, and Honest Charts
module_description: Module 26 teaches analytical communication: graph visualization discipline (Gephi/igraph/ForceAtlas), temporal charts and small multiples for topic trends, honest charting (axes, uncertainty, sample sizes), and building interactive dashboards (Streamlit, Shiny, Power BI/Tableau, or Observable). Students produce a dashboard and a one-page insight memo - the standard entry-level job test format.
core_concepts: Visual encoding choices and honesty in charts
learning_outcomes: C3 Produce a multi-panel visualization of a social dataset
C4 Build an interactive dashboard for a listening question
C5 Write an insight memo that only claims what the data supports
methods_models: Graph layouts (ForceAtlas), aggregation and smoothing, small multiples, interactive filtering, uncertainty display
evaluation_metrics: Not model metrics; rubric on clarity, honesty, and completeness; peer review scoring
pitfalls_limitations: Cherry-picked windows, truncated axes, over-plotting, interpreting layout position as meaning, dashboards that hide uncertainty
tools_stack: matplotlib/seaborn, plotly, igraph + Gephi, streamlit, shiny (R), tableau public or power BI (teaching licences vary)
commercial_platforms: Tableau Public and Power BI demos
tools_access_cost: BI teaching licences vary by institution; open-source tools are free
lab_activities: Build a dashboard on the course dataset with at least one network view and one temporal view
assessment_methods: Dashboard plus one-page insight memo, peer-reviewed against a rubric; graded on clarity, honesty and completeness
data_collection_workflow: Collect -> clean -> aggregate per unit/time -> build dashboard -> write insight memo -> preserve data and code
textbooks: Healy, Data Visualization: A Practical Introduction (2018)
trends_2024_2026: 2024-2026: LLM-generated narrative reports and agentic dashboards changed the analyst's job toward auditing generated claims, so visualization teaching now includes verification habits
industry_relevance: Dashboard and insight-reporting skills are the most common entry-level requirement for analyst roles; students leave with a portfolio dashboard plus a one-page insight memo, which is the standard job-test format for insights teams.
localization_context: Indonesian-language data (local issues, local brands) is used so the dashboard and narrative are in Bahasa Indonesia, matching the reporting language of local clients and courses' capstone sponsors.
ethics_regulation: Honest charting (no truncated axes, no cherry-picked windows), privacy-safe display of user-level data, and clear separation of observed metrics from inferred claims.
case_study_scenarios: Build a live dashboard tracking an Indonesian issue across platforms for a capstone client.
